D.t: Chris Coons leads by 27.4 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 114,677 votes; a one point swing is about 2,090 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +18.6 and D +36.1. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The biggest vote banks for Democrats: New Castle, a projected net 110,467 votes; Kent, a projected net 9,123 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Sussex, R +4.2, 28.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Chris Coons runs furthest behind in Sussex, Kent. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 73% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.66 points; Men, 46% of voters, 60 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.27 points; Midsize counties, 45% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.25 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Chris Coons: Immigration voters 30 to 68, Midsize counties 52 to 46, Incomes $125K and up 58 to 40. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
